Section: Whole genome sequencing data

Whole genome sequencing was a laboratory process that determines the order of nucleotides in an organism's DNA. Our WGS data for patient cohorts with MDS were conducted by Broad Institute using a modified version of the Illumina TruSeq PCR-Free LT Library Prep method (Illumina).
Briefly, 3-4ug gDNA was fragmented via Covaris acoustic shearing to a size of 900-1000bp. Sheared samples were then dual size selected using AMPure XP beads (Beckman Coulter) to first select for larger fragments, and secondly to select out small fragments. End repair followed the
standard Illumina protocol. Following End repair, a second dual size selection, identical to the first, was conducted to further select for the correct fragment size. Adenylation and Adapter ligation followed the Illumina standard protocol. Following adapter ligation, a final set of two AMPure washes
was completed to purify final whole genome libraries. Final qualification and quantification of libraries was conducted on a Fragment Analyzer (Advanced Analytical) and via qPCR using Universal qPCR MasterMix (Kapa Biosystems) on a CFX384 quantitative thermalcycler (Bio-Rad). Libraries
were pooled at 3uM and sequenced via Illumina MiSeq to QC for cluster density yield and index distribution. Samples were then normalized to appropriate concentration to load on the Illumina Novaseq 6000 (Illumina) using 2x150 paired-end sequencing on an S4 flowcell. Pool size was 12
samples to achieve the required 60x depth minimum for each sample. The raw bam files were generated with hg38 references.

Section: Genomic variation definition

Germline variant: A variant in a reproductive cell (egg or sperm) that is in the DNA of every cell in the offspring's body, which can be passed from parent to offspring and is, therefore, hereditary.
Somatic variant: A DNA alteration that occurs after conception in any cell of the body, except for germ cells (sperm and egg).
Single nucleotide variant (SNV): A DNA sequence variation that occurs when a single nucleotide (adenine, thymine, cytosine, or guanine) in the genome sequence is altered. Single nucleotide variants may be rare or common in a population.
Insertion-deletion (Indel): A type of genetic variation that occurs when a nucleotide sequence is inserted or deleted in the genome.
Structural variant (SV): A variation in the structure of an organism's DNA that can range in size from 50 to over a million base pairs, such as deletions, duplications, insertions, inversions and translocations.
Non synonymous mutation: A specific type of genetic mutation that alters the amino acid sequence of a protein, such as missense, splicing, frameshift, nonsense mutations.
Noncoding variant: A genetic variant that occurs in noncoding DNA, which is DNA that does not code for amino acids.

Section: Genomic sequencing specification

Chromosome (Chrom): The Chromosome number.
Position (POS): The genomic coordinates.
Genotype (GT): A specific combination of genetic variant alleles at a particular gene locus, such as wild type, heterozygous or homozygous.
Quality (Qual): The quality scores from the variant calling tool.
Read depth (DP): The number of reads at a specific position.
Variant allele frequency (VAF): A measure of the proportion of variant alleles in a genetic locus.
Breakpoint: A location in a genomic sequence where related sequences are not collinear and cannot be globally aligned.
Copy number: The number of copies of a particular sequence of DNA present in the genome of an individual.

Section: Genomic file format

FASTQ: A standard format of text-based file that stores NGS sequences from the clusters that pass filter on a flow cell and their corresponding quality scores (http://gorgonzola.cshl.edu/pfb/2011/public/ohofmann/Papers/PDF_FASTQ.pdf).
SAM: A tab-delimited text format consisting of a header section and an alignment section from sequence alignment/map (https://samtools.github.io/hts-specs/SAMv1.pdf).
BAM: A compressed binary version of a SAM file that is used to represent aligned sequences.
CRAM (Compressed Read Archive) : A highly compressed, reference-based file format for storing DNA sequencing data
BED: A text file format used to store genomic regions as coordinates and associated annotations (https://samtools.github.io/hts-specs/BEDv1.pdf).
VCF: A text file that stores and reports genomic sequence variations (https://samtools.github.io/hts-specs/VCFv4.2.pdf).

Section: Reference genome

A human genome reference sequence is an accepted representation of the human genome sequence that is used by researchers as a standard for comparison to DNA sequences generated in their studies. It aims to provide the highest-quality, best possible consensus representations of the
sequence and structural diversity found in the human genome among populations.
